chapter: Central High, first records and leaving home
title: The little school band, her boyfriend Sprat Morton and Bill Beason
summary: After the tape turns over, she describes how tight the little band was. Her childhood boyfriend was trumpeter Bernise 'Sprat' Morton, who later played with Roy Eldridge in Horace Henderson's band but got no farther than Buffalo; drummer Bill Beason later played with Chick Webb.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: (TAPE # 1 SIDE B)
Here we go again. We're going to talk about that little band. I know everybody was pretty tight in that little Band, weren't they?
Oh yeah, everybody was. It was nice. The boys, they were alot of fun. And it was just a nice group to be around.
You had one special guy?
Yeah, my childhood bow was a trumpet player.
What was his name?
His name was Bernise Morton and they used to call him "sprat".
"Sprat"?
Yeah.
How do you spell that, s-p-r-a-t, sprat?
Yeah. And he was a very rich trumpet player then. And Jonah and Dicky, and Bill and all of them.

Bill Beason?
Yeah. They always used to play together?
Did they? They had their own little group?
Yeah, and they had a dance band later.
Well that's wonderful. Bill Beason, and that's the drummer that was with Chick?
Yes.
After he came to New York?
Oh yes.
A very good drummer.
He certainly was a very good drummer. He was one of the great ones. I don't know how he got out of the business or why he got out. He was really good.
And you said that Bernise blew horn with Roy (Eldridge) too, you said, didn't you?
Yeah. He and Roy were in Horace Henderson's band together.
Oh, but he never came to New York?
